result.summary: This is a mixed-use urban street with continuous sidewalks and on-street parallel parking on both sides. A midblock crossing is indicated by signage and dashed pavement markings, though it lacks high-visibility paint or curb extensions.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb line block the sight lines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to use the midblock crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street near the dashed pavement markings.

hazards.name: Low-visibility crossing markings
hazards.description: The midblock crossing uses dashed transverse lines which are less visible to approaching drivers than continental or zebra markings.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace the dashed lines with continental or zebra-style markings to increase the visibility of the crossing zone.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crossing to ensure clear sight lines.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a continuous, paved sidewalk in good condition, separated from the narrow roadway by a curb and parallel parking. The street is lined with buildings directly at the sidewalk edge, including a stone church, creating a well-defined urban corridor.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars, particularly the large black vehicle in the foreground, obstruct the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the ends of the block to improve sightlines for pedestrians entering the roadway.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Install street trees to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the street and to encourage slower driving speeds through vertical enclosure.

result.summary: The image shows a typical urban street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and parallel on-street parking. While the environment is walkable, it lacks visible pedestrian safety enhancements such as marked crossings or traffic calming measures in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates a visual barrier between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbsides throughout the visible block

hazards.name: Lack of Designated Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks over a long stretch of street may lead to unpredictable mid-block crossing behavior.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near intersections or potential crossing points to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is severely constrained by an extremely narrow sidewalk that is further obstructed by parked vehicles and debris. There is a complete lack of pedestrian-specific safety infrastructure such as marked crossings or buffers from traffic, likely forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Severely Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk width between the building railing and parked cars is insufficient for safe pedestrian passage, likely failing ADA standards.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the red building frontage behind the parked cars

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bags and a utility pole further block the already limited walking space, creating tripping hazards and forcing people into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: On the sidewalk to the right of the white car

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Reallocate road space from the parking lane to widen the sidewalk to a minimum of 6 feet of clear path.

interventions.title: Parking Removal/Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove on-street parking in this specific section to clear the walkway and improve sightlines for pedestrians and drivers.
